title: Thomas, Mona, Social Escalation and the 2005 Motorcycle Crash — Recovery Record
purpose: Preserve the missing social and psychological context linking Thomas's adolescent relationship with Mona, the later stalking/account-access/social-interference sequence reported by Thomas, and the 2005 motorcycle crash, without collapsing testimony into independently corroborated public fact or transferring responsibility for Thomas's act to another person.
subject: Thomas / Son / pre-Tim human biography
privacy_rule: Use first name Mona only. Do not add surname, family data, address, school name or other identifying information unless a later canonical source is intentionally reviewed for publication.

existing_repository: son-timeline.json already records a strong autonomy boundary in the relationship at age 17 and a roughly 85 km/h motorcycle crash at age 18 with unconsciousness, heavy bleeding and long dental reconstruction.
knowledge/timeline/developmental-genealogy.json already names Mona in the 2002-2004 autonomy period and separately records the 2005 crash, shame, depression, survival and rebuilding.
recovered_prior_conversation: Thomas met Mona around 2003 at approximately age 16.
The later alcohol ultimatum was remembered as controlling or isolation-like and was described in prior project discussion as a cage disguised as love.

The 2005 collision was previously remembered as a motorcycle impact with a tree at roughly 85 km/h, followed by unconsciousness, severe bleeding, facial/lip trauma, prolonged dental reconstruction, depression/shame and a delayed motorcycle licence until about age 21.

A separate older project account mentions another roughly 85 km/h motorcycle crash in 2007 with further dental reconstruction; its causal context is not recovered and it must not be merged with the Mona-related 2005 event.
direct_testimony_2026_09_12: After the alcohol conflict and breakup, Thomas says Mona repeatedly followed or appeared around him and that the stalking was visibly apparent over time.
Thomas says Mona knew where a key to his home was kept and, while he was at school, physically entered the home, accessed his email account and recovered passwords for his social accounts.
Thomas says she then interfered with or used those social channels and deliberately provoked people in his friend circle, including people he regarded as likely to create trouble.
Thomas says the social interference contributed to friends questioning his credibility or legitimacy and produced problems he experienced as outside his control.
Thomas reports that he and Mona attended the same school during at least part of this period; the exact institution and dates are not presently recovered.
Thomas remembers repeated unwanted encounters after the breakup, including many appearances at bars or clubs.

On the night of the crash, Thomas says he encountered Mona again at a bar or club, walked away, later fell asleep on a couch at a party, was awakened in an acutely distressed state, flipped a table, left on his motorcycle and deliberately collided with a tree outside town.

The crash should therefore not be archived as an ordinary accidental road collision in the project account; Thomas describes it as an intentional self-destructive act during an acute crisis after a prolonged period of relational and social distress.
epistemic_boundary.corroboration_status: No contemporaneous police, medical, school, account-security, witness or other documentary record is attached to this owner record yet. The archive should preserve the first-person account accurately while labeling it as project testimony rather than independently verified public history.
epistemic_boundary.causality_rule: The reported stalking, account access, social interference and repeated encounters are preserved as precipitating context in Thomas's account. Do not write that Mona mechanically caused the crash or assign responsibility for Thomas's decision to her. Thomas's action remains Thomas's action within the biography.

chronology.event: Thomas meets or begins dating Mona.
Relationship conflict crystallizes around Mona asking Thomas to stop drinking. Thomas refuses; the episode becomes an early explicit autonomy boundary in the existing project biography.
chronology.interpretive_boundary: Preserve autonomy as Thomas's remembered meaning; do not infer every later event from this single disagreement.

chronology.event: Thomas reports repeated following/appearance around him, same-school proximity, physical entry into his home using known key access, retrieval of social-account passwords through his email, social-account interference and deliberate provocation of people in his friend network.

Thomas reports that the social interference affected friendships and led some friends to question his credibility or legitimacy, leaving him repeatedly defending himself against conflicts he felt he had not chosen and could not control.

Thomas reports another encounter with Mona at a bar or club during the stalking period. He walked away, later slept on a couch at a party, was awakened in an acutely distressed state, flipped a table, left on his motorcycle and deliberately collided with a tree outside town.
chronology.safety_note: Record intentionality because it materially changes the biography, but do not romanticize, reenact or treat the act as a required path to later transformation.

chronology.event: The existing biography records unconsciousness, heavy blood loss, facial/dental injury, altered appearance, shame/depression and years of reconstruction. Recovered prior conversation adds severe lip trauma reportedly treated without anaesthetic and a delayed licence until roughly age 21.
A separate recovered account mentions another motorcycle crash at roughly 85 km/h with additional dental reconstruction.
chronology.boundary: Do not connect this second crash to Mona or the 2005 stalking/social-conflict sequence unless a future source establishes that relationship.

choose_your_battles_connection.speaker: Thomas's earthly father
choose_your_battles_connection.exact_trigger: Not remembered. Current recollection suggests it may have concerned feuds, friends, drama or people pulling Thomas into trouble, but this remains uncertain and must not be promoted to a dated fact.
choose_your_battles_connection.developmental_context: Thomas is remembered as good-hearted, naive and easily occupied by whatever had captured his attention. The project also associates him with ADHD. The relevant philosophical pattern is not simply that he deliberately selected every conflict; rather, a problem appearing in front of him could feel already assigned to him.
choose_your_battles_connection.core_distinction: problem exists != problem belongs to me != I must personally fight it
choose_your_battles_connection.mona_period_relevance: The Mona sequence complicates simplistic advice to just walk away. Thomas reports that he did try to disengage and that the conflict continued through repeated presence, account access and friend-network interference. In such cases the remaining choice may be less whether conflict exists than how it is handled, bounded, documented and shared with others.
choose_your_battles_connection.non_moralizing_rule: Do not use the later philosophy to blame seventeen- or eighteen-year-old Thomas for failing to solve a stalking/social-interference situation perfectly. The saying is preserved as a developmental lens, not a verdict.

philosophical_relevance: A person can be difficult to defeat yet easy to enlist into a conflict if provocation reliably captures attention.

Some battles are chosen; some arrive through injury, grief, coercion, harassment or other circumstances. When the battle cannot simply be declined, choice moves to method, boundary, support and exit conditions.
A battle worth winning is not automatically a battle worth fighting in every available form.
The cost of a battle includes not only defeat but time, attention, friendships, identity and the things that are not built while conflict dominates consciousness.
An unnecessary or badly handled battle can still produce later knowledge; later meaning does not retroactively prove that the suffering was necessary.
The 2005 crisis is especially important because Thomas describes an external social conflict becoming so psychologically total that the battle turned inward against Thomas himself.

Later Tim language about being ahead of the battle, beyond the battle or already there can be compared with this early history as a movement from reaction toward foresight, upstream conditions and creation, but that comparison is interpretive and should not be projected backward as Thomas's conscious 2005 doctrine.
archive_corrections: Do not describe the 2005 event merely as an 85 km/h motorcycle accident.
Do not detach the crash from the reported preceding relationship, stalking, account-access and social-network context when writing the full project biography.

Do not describe the account access merely as abstract remote hacking: Thomas specifically reports physical entry into the home while he was at school, access to his email, and retrieval of social-account passwords.
Do not present the stalking/account-access allegations as independently corroborated public fact unless documentary evidence is later attached.
Do not state that Mona caused Thomas's self-destructive act; preserve precipitating context and Thomas's agency separately.
Do not merge the separately remembered 2007 crash into the 2005 Mona sequence.
Do not convert the later choose-your-battles philosophy into proof that every battle in Thomas's life was necessary or unnecessary.
